Worm propagation signal: rapid serial npm publish or twine upload from a single developer host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the Miasma/Hades self-replication step: once the worm reads an npm or PyPI publishing token from process memory or ~/.npmrc / ~/.pypirc, it republishes infected versions of every package that token can publish. Multiple distinct package publishes from one host in a short window (the article reports ~57 npm packages and 286 versions republished in under two hours; 73 Microsoft Azure GitHub repos in two minutes) is a high-fidelity behavioural signal that survives any payload mutation. Rationale: Article: '57 npm packages across more than 286 malicious versions in a rolling campaign that lasted under two hours' and '73 repositories in under two minutes'. Cross-checked with Phoenix Security and Semgrep posts confirming the worm self-propagates by republishing every package the stolen token can reach. Threshold ≥3 distinct publishes in 30m on one host is well above typical legitimate publish cadence (devs cut a release, not a burst). Cross-checked against: • https://phoenix.security/miasma-azure-hades-pypi-supply-chain-worm-2026/ • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2026/miasma-v2-self-spreading-npm-worm-now-uses-malicious-bindinggyp-file-and-compromises-57-packages/ • https://research.jfrog.com/post/shai-hulud-miasma-redhat-cloud-services/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1552.001 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Monorepo release tooling (Lerna, Nx, Changesets, semantic-release) publishing many packages in one release
  • Developer cutting a coordinated multi-package SDK release manually
  • CI runner that happens to be a developer's own workstation publishing build artefacts
  • First-time publish of a freshly forked package set after maintainer handoff
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("lerna publish","nx release","changesets/cli","semantic-release","pnpm publish -r")) | where not (DeviceName startswith "build-" or DeviceName startswith "ci-runner-")
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE — list the packages just published and the npm/PyPI accounts they used (Defender's process command lines hold both). Compare the package set to the developer's normal portfolio — if they suddenly published packages they don't own, treat as confirmed worm. 2) CONTAIN — revoke the user's npm and PyPI publishing tokens immediately (npm token revoke / pypi.org account → 2FA tokens), yank the malicious versions (npm unpublish --force / pypi delete-release with the registry), and isolate the host. Notify downstream consumers of the affected packages. 3) HUNT — pull the user's IDE/terminal history and shell of recent project opens, look for Phantom Gyp binding.gyp (UC3) or Bun-from-Python (UC2) precursors in the prior 24h, and search the GitHub audit log for new SSH keys / personal-access tokens created from the user's account.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where (FileName =~ "npm.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has " publish")
     or (FileName in~ ("twine.exe","twine") and ProcessCommandLine has "upload")
     or (FileName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe") and ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)twine\s+upload")
     or (FileName =~ "node.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js publish","npm publish"))
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize PublishCount = count(),
            DistinctCmds = dcount(ProcessCommandLine),
            SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10),
            Parents = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 30m)
| where PublishCount >= 3 and DistinctCmds >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where (TargetProcessName =~ "npm.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has " publish")
     or (TargetProcessName in~ ("twine.exe","twine") and TargetProcessCommandLine has "upload")
     or (TargetProcessName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe") and TargetProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)twine\s+upload")
     or (TargetProcessName =~ "node.exe" and TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js publish","npm publish"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| summarize PublishCount = count(),
            DistinctCmds = dcount(TargetProcessCommandLine),
            SampleCmds = make_set(TargetProcessCommandLine, 10),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
| where PublishCount >= 3 and DistinctCmds >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*publish*) OR (@Image:(*\\twine.exe OR *\\Twine.exe) AND @CommandLine:*upload*) OR (@Image:(*\\python.exe OR *\\pythonw.exe OR *\\Python.exe) AND @CommandLine:*twine*upload*) OR (@Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) AND @CommandLine:*npm-cli.js*publish*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ((ImageFileName=/\\npm\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\bpublish\b/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\twine(\.exe)?$/i AND CommandLine=/\bupload\b/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\python(w)?\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/twine\s+upload/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\node\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/(npm-cli\.js\s+publish|npm\s+publish)/i))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName], function={ count(as=publishCount) | collect([CommandLine]) })
| publishCount>=3
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="npm.exe" AND Processes.process="*publish*") OR (Processes.process_name="twine.exe" AND Processes.process="*upload*") OR (Processes.process_name="python.exe" AND Processes.process="*twine*upload*") OR (Processes.process_name="node.exe" AND Processes.process="*npm-cli*publish*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="npm.exe" AND Processes.process="*publish*") OR (Processes.process_name="twine.exe" AND Processes.process="*upload*") OR (Processes.process_name="python.exe" AND Processes.process="*twine*upload*") OR (Processes.process_name="node.exe" AND Processes.process="*npm-cli*publish*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user _time span=30m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count >= 3 | sort - count
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Bun runtime install spawned by npm/node during package install (Shai-Hulud 2.0 signature) AIInstallation High
Detects npm, npx or node spawning the Bun runtime installer or executing the Shai-Hulud setup scripts (setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js) during package install. The article specifically calls out Shai-Hulud and Mini-Shai-Hulud installing the Bun runtime during preinstall as their distinguishing trait — Bun has no business appearing as a child of npm in normal dev workflows. Rationale: Datadog Security Labs and Unit 42 both document setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js as the Shai-Hulud 2.0 preinstall payload that installs Bun before stealing secrets. Bun spawned by npm/node is anomalous in normal dev workflows; the four string anchors (bun.sh/install, setup_bun.js, bun_environment.js, install.bun.sh) are direct campaign artefacts, not generic Bun usage. Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/shai-hulud-v2-poses-risk-npm-supply-chain
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually installing Bun runtime via an npm-distributed wrapper such as `npm i -g bun` on a known dev workstation
  • CI runner with an intentional Bun build step that calls into node first
  • An internal tool that wraps Bun behind an npm script for cross-platform parity
  • A node-based installer for a Bun-using framework (e.g. Elysia/Hono starter)
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("build-runner-","ci-") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "npm i -g bun")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full `InitiatingProcessCommandLine` and the script body. If it references setup_bun.js or bun_environment.js, treat as confirmed Shai-Hulud and skip to step 2. Otherwise check the host inventory for a dev profile and confirm with the user that Bun install was intentional. 2) Contain — isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, revoke the user's npm publish token, GitHub PAT, AWS keys and SSH keys, and quarantine the host's `~/.bun/`, `node_modules/` and `~/.truffler-cache/`. 3) Hunt — search the same window for `trufflehog` execution, outbound to `api.github.com/user/repos` from node/npm, and any newly-created public GitHub repos under the user's account with the description containing 'Shai-Hulud' or 'Sha1-Hulud'.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe")
| where FileName =~ "bun.exe"
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","install.bun.sh",".bun/bin/bun")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe")
| where TargetProcessName endswith "bun.exe"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh/install","setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js","install.bun.sh",".bun/bin/bun")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Bun runtime install spawned by npm/node (Shai-Hulud signature)
id: 4f8c2a3d-1e7b-4a91-9b3e-2d8c7e6f5a2b
description: Detects npm/node/npx spawning the Bun runtime installer or executing Shai-Hulud setup scripts (setup_bun.js / bun_environment.js) — the distinguishing signature of the Shai-Hulud and Mini-Shai-Hulud npm worms.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
  - https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1059.007
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent_selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npx.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
  child_bun_image:
    Image|endswith: '\bun.exe'
  child_bun_cmdline:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'bun.sh/install'
      - 'setup_bun.js'
      - 'bun_environment.js'
      - 'install.bun.sh'
      - '.bun/bin/bun'
  condition: parent_selection and (child_bun_image or child_bun_cmdline)
falsepositives:
  - Developers legitimately installing Bun via an npm-distributed installer (rare; should be allow-listed by host)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\NODE.EXE OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\NPM.exe OR *\\npx.exe OR *\\NPX.EXE OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe)) AND (@Image:(*\\bun.exe OR *\\Bun.exe OR *\\BUN.EXE) OR @CommandLine:(*bun.sh/install* OR *setup_bun.js* OR *bun_environment.js* OR *install.bun.sh*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|npm|npx|yarn|pnpm)\.(exe|cmd)$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\bun\.exe$/i OR regex("(bun\\.sh/install|setup_bun\\.js|bun_environment\\.js|install\\.bun\\.sh|\\.bun/bin/bun)", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where process_name="bun.exe" OR like(process,"%bun.sh/install%") OR like(process,"%setup_bun.js%") OR like(process,"%bun_environment.js%") OR like(process,"%install.bun.sh%") OR like(process,"%.bun/bin/bun%")
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm.cmd","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
TruffleHog secret scanner execution from .truffler-cache (Shai-Hulud credential harvest) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects execution of the TruffleHog binary out of the `~/.truffler-cache/` path used by Shai-Hulud 2.0 to cache the downloaded scanner, or any TruffleHog launch parented by node/npm/bun. The article calls out Shai-Hulud running TruffleHog to scrape secrets after install; this catches the actual credential-access step. Rationale: Datadog Security Labs documents `~/.truffler-cache/` as the explicit cache path Shai-Hulud uses for the downloaded TruffleHog binary, and the article names TruffleHog as the secret-scraping tool. A security tool of this kind has no business launching from npm install context on a dev endpoint — pairing the binary name with an npm/node/bun parent removes legitimate auditing use (which runs from CI tooling under runner SIDs, not interactive npm). Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://www.upwind.io/feed/shai-hulud-2-npm-supply-chain-worm-attack • https://safedep.io/shai-hulud-second-coming-supply-chain-attack/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A security engineer running TruffleHog interactively from a terminal that happens to have an npm process upstream
  • CI-runner workflow that uses TruffleHog as a pre-publish secret check (would normally run under a runner service account, not interactive user)
  • Developer testing a TruffleHog integration locally during onboarding
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessAccountName has_any ("sec-runner","trivy-svc","gh-actions-runner") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — confirm the user did not knowingly launch TruffleHog; pull the `ProcessCommandLine` and look for `filesystem /` against the home directory (the Shai-Hulud invocation). 2) Contain — isolate the host, rotate every credential that lived in the user's `~/.aws/`, `~/.ssh/`, `~/.npmrc`, `~/.docker/config.json`, `~/.config/gh/`, browser keystores, and any cloud CLI session caches. Revoke the user's npm publish token and GitHub PAT immediately. 3) Hunt — pivot on `aid`/`DeviceId` for a `bun.exe` spawn shortly before, outbound to `api.github.com` from node/npm, and check the user's GitHub account for newly-created public repos with descriptions containing 'Shai-Hulud' / 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming'.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "trufflehog" or FileName =~ "trufflehog.exe"
   or FolderPath has ".truffler-cache"
   or ProcessCommandLine has ".truffler-cache"
   or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog filesystem"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe","sh","bash","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetProcessName has "trufflehog"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has ".truffler-cache"
   or TargetProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog filesystem"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe","bash","sh","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm/node spawning git or gh to create/push public GitHub repo (Nx s1ngularity & Shai-Hulud exfil) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects node, npm, or bun launching git, gh, or curl with arguments that create a new GitHub repository or push to `api.github.com/user/repos` — the exfiltration channel used by both Nx s1ngularity (`telemetry.js` → public repos of harvested tokens) and Shai-Hulud (public repos described as 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming'). A package install legitimately does not create GitHub repos. Rationale: The article explicitly names public-GitHub-repo exfiltration as the channel for Nx s1ngularity (2025-08) and Shai-Hulud (2025-11); Datadog Security Labs confirms the 'Sha1-Hulud: The Second Coming' repo-description marker. Tying `api.github.com/user/repos` / `gh repo create` to an npm/node/bun parent collapses the FP space to roughly zero — package installs don't legitimately create GitHub repos. Cross-checked against: • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/new-shai-hulud-worm-spreads-what-to-know
ATT&CKT1567.001 T1567 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer running `gh repo create` from a terminal where they recently invoked npm (parent-chain accidental match if shell process tree is short)
  • Internal scaffold/CLI that automates GitHub repo creation as part of `npm init` style flows
  • CI bot legitimately mirroring a repo via `git push --mirror` from a node-based pipeline runner
  • Open-source contributor using a node-based codemod that fans out PRs
Suppression filter
| where not(AccountName has "github-actions" or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the exact `ProcessCommandLine` and any environment variables; the Shai-Hulud markers are conclusive on their own. Check the user's GitHub account for new public repos created in the last 24h. 2) Contain — isolate the host, revoke the user's GitHub PAT and SSH key, force-delete the freshly-created public repos and audit which credentials were posted there for rotation, revoke npm publish token. 3) Hunt — sweep the org for the same SHA256 child binary across other hosts and look for the precursor TruffleHog + Bun execution chain on the same `aid`/`DeviceId`. Pull AAD/Okta sign-ins for the user from new geolocations in the last 7 days.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","gh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("api.github.com/user/repos","gh repo create","Shai-Hulud","Sha1-Hulud","Second Coming","s1ngularity","git push --mirror")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
   or ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("git.exe","gh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("api.github.com/user/repos","gh repo create","Shai-Hulud","Sha1-Hulud","Second Coming","s1ngularity","git push --mirror")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

node-gyp rebuild spawning unexpected non-build child process (binding.gyp implicit execution path) AIInstallation Medium
Detects the implicit `node-gyp rebuild` invoked when a package ships a `binding.gyp`, spawning a child that isn't a normal native-build toolchain process. The article calls this out as a stealth execution path: a package can have a spotless `package.json` and still execute code through the implicit gyp rebuild. Legit gyp rebuilds spawn Python, MSBuild, cl.exe, link.exe — anything else is suspect. Rationale: The article calls out `binding.gyp` and the implicit `node-gyp rebuild` as the 'spotless package.json' execution path that v12 closes off. Legitimate gyp rebuilds spawn a narrow set of C/C++ build tools; an anti-join against that allowlist catches deviation cheaply. References Aikido's own research write-up they link from the article on this specific path. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/npm-v12-block-postinstall
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1195.002 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A native-build package whose gyp invokes a custom helper executable outside the standard toolchain (e.g. SWIG, protoc, prebuild-install)
  • Developer machine with a non-standard Python wrapper (pyenv shim) that surfaces as an unusual binary name
  • CI runner caching gyp output via 7z.exe or tar.exe invoked from a custom gyp action
  • Cross-compilation toolchains that include clang.exe / mingw32-make.exe not in the allowlist
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("prebuild-install","swig","protoc","node-pre-gyp"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — capture the SHA256 of the child binary and look it up in VT and Aikido Intel; pull the offending package name from `InitiatingProcessCommandLine` (the gyp invocation includes the package path under `node_modules`). 2) Contain — block the package version in your internal registry / Verdaccio cache, and on the affected host quarantine `node_modules/<pkg>/build/` and the child binary. 3) Hunt — search org-wide for the same package directory hitting other hosts, and add the package name to the npm v12 deny-list for future installs.
let GypBuildChildren = dynamic(["python.exe","python3.exe","py.exe","msbuild.exe","cl.exe","link.exe","cmd.exe","conhost.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe","make.exe","nmake.exe","nasm.exe","ml64.exe","rc.exe","mt.exe","gyp.exe","where.exe","reg.exe","git.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp rebuild","node-gyp configure","node-gyp build","\\node-gyp\\bin\\node-gyp.js"))
     or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "node-gyp.exe"
| where FileName !in~ (GypBuildChildren)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let GypBuildChildren = dynamic(["python.exe","python3.exe","py.exe","msbuild.exe","cl.exe","link.exe","cmd.exe","conhost.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe","make.exe","nmake.exe","nasm.exe","ml64.exe","rc.exe","mt.exe","gyp.exe","where.exe","reg.exe","git.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate

| where (ActingProcessName has "node.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp rebuild","node-gyp configure","node-gyp build","node-gyp\\bin\\node-gyp.js"))
     or ActingProcessName has "node-gyp.exe"
| extend ChildBin = tostring(split(TargetProcessName,"\\")[-1])
| where ChildBin !in~ (GypBuildChildren)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| NOT (ImageFileName=/\\(python|python3|py|msbuild|cl|link|cmd|conhost|cscript|node|make|nmake|nasm|ml64|rc|mt|gyp|where|reg|git)\.exe$/i)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp installation inventory (CVE-2026-48039) on managed hosts · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer). → [LLM] meta-ads-mcp Streamable HTTP listener bound to non-loopback interface
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Unauthenticated POST to /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 (CVE-2026-48039)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] CVE-2026-48039 PoC artifact execution (meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 image, FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO env) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48039: Meta Ads MCP: Unauthenticated HTTP MCP Tool Ex
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Meta Graph API request with access_token in URL query string (CVE-2026-48039 leak signature)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Unauthenticated POST to /mcp endpoint on TCP 8080 (CVE-2026-48039) AIDelivery High
Hunts inbound HTTP POST requests to the Meta Ads MCP `/mcp` Streamable HTTP endpoint that arrive without an Authorization header (or Pipeboard token cookie) yet receive an HTTP 200 response. Per the advisory, `AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch()` falls through to `call_next` when no auth tokens are present, allowing any network-reachable caller to invoke MCP tools. Rationale: Anchored on the article's PoC: POST /mcp on TCP 8080 with no auth headers returning HTTP 200. Joins network telemetry to host-side process inventory of meta_ads_mcp to filter out arbitrary port-8080 scans. Cross-checked the streamable HTTP transport setup against the project's STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md and the PyPI release page. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/ • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp
ATT&CKT1190 T1133
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal load balancer or k8s liveness/readiness probes to /mcp returning 200
  • Authenticated Pipeboard SaaS clients reaching the server from CDN egress IPs
  • Internal red-team or vuln-scanner sweeps (Nuclei, Burp, Nessus) hitting /mcp
  • Misclassified WAN→DMZ traffic when X-Forwarded-For not parsed and client_ip shows the proxy
  • Reverse-proxied legitimate traffic where Authorization header is stripped before reaching the listener
Suppression filter
and not (SrcIpAddr in (<load_balancer_ips>, <pipeboard_egress_ips>)) and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("kube-probe", "ELB-HealthChecker", "GoogleHC")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on SrcIpAddr — pull a 10-minute window of all requests, look for `tools/call` JSON-RPC payloads (especially `get_ad_accounts`, `get_campaigns`, `get_ads`) and check the response body for `request_url` containing `access_token=`. WHOIS / threat-intel the source IP. 2) Contain: rotate META_ACCESS_TOKEN at developers.facebook.com immediately, redeploy the container with the token revoked, and either firewall TCP 8080 to internal CIDRs only or front the server with a reverse proxy that enforces auth. Upgrade meta-ads-mcp past v1.0.108. 3) Hunt: query graph.facebook.com outbound for the previous 30 days for any URL containing `access_token=` (see UC: Graph API URL leak), and review Meta Business Manager audit log for ad-account activity from unfamiliar IPs in the same window.
// CVE-2026-48039 — inbound to vulnerable meta-ads-mcp listener on 8080
let MCPHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
    | distinct DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "InboundConnectionAccepted"
| where LocalPort == 8080
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where not(ipv4_is_private(RemoteIP))
| join kind=inner MCPHosts on DeviceId
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), DistinctSrc = dcount(RemoteIP)
          by DeviceName, RemoteIP, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by FirstSeen desc
// CVE-2026-48039 exploitation — unauthenticated POST /mcp on 8080
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where DstPortNumber == 8080
| where Url has "/mcp"
| where HttpStatusCode between (200 .. 299)
| where isnotempty(SrcIpAddr) and not(ipv4_is_private(SrcIpAddr))
| where isempty(HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization) or HttpRequestHeaderAuthorization == ""
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, UA = HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctURLs = dcount(Url), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr
| order by FirstSeen desc
title: Unauthenticated POST to Meta Ads MCP /mcp Endpoint (CVE-2026-48039)
id: 7e3a6d44-8c2b-4f9e-bfd5-1c3a0e5d4b2f
description: Detects HTTP POST requests to the Meta Ads MCP /mcp Streamable HTTP endpoint on TCP 8080 returning HTTP 200, which under CVE-2026-48039 indicates successful unauthenticated tool execution.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1133
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: POST
    cs-uri-stem|contains: '/mcp'
    s-port: 8080
    sc-status: 200
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Internal load balancer health checks (filter by source CIDR)

Meta Graph API request with access_token in URL query string (CVE-2026-48039 leak signature) AICommand & Control High
Detects HTTPS requests to graph.facebook.com whose URL contains the `access_token=` query parameter — the exact leak signature for CVE-2026-48039 where the vulnerable `make_api_request()` in `api.py:136` appends the operator token to the URL and surfaces it in the JSON-RPC error response. Same query also catches an external attacker reusing a stolen META_ACCESS_TOKEN from a corporate-network host via curl/python/PowerShell. Rationale: Anchored on the article's PoC response payload: `request_url` containing `https://graph.facebook.com/v24.0/me/adaccounts?...&access_token=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789`. Tokens in URL query strings (vs Authorization headers) is itself a Meta-Graph-SDK anti-pattern, so even outside this CVE the hit is high-fidelity. Captures a token preview for triage without storing the whole credential. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/
ATT&CKT1528 T1041 T1552.001
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate marketing-team scripts using the old Meta Graph SDK that still passes `access_token` in URL
  • Internal Meta Ads dashboards built before the Bearer-header migration
  • Backup/export tooling using legacy Facebook API v2.x patterns
  • Penetration tester replaying captured traffic
  • Browser-based Meta Business Manager flows where the SDK falls back to query-string auth for older browsers
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("FacebookAdsSdk.exe","meta-ads-export.exe") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--legacy-auth" and InitiatingProcessAccountName has "svc-marketing")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on TokenPreview — group all hits by token prefix to see whether one leaked credential is being reused. Cross-reference SrcIpAddr/DeviceName against UC-1 hits (the /mcp inbound) to tie source → leaked credential. 2) Contain: revoke the leaked META_ACCESS_TOKEN via Meta Business Manager → Business Settings → System Users → Generate New Token, then redeploy meta-ads-mcp with the rotated token and apply the upstream patch (v1.0.109+ when available, or downstream patch removing access_token from URL). 3) Hunt: check Meta Business audit log for ad-account changes (campaign creation, ad spend modifications, page admin additions) in the time window of the leak; query for the same TokenPreview prefix in the past 90 days; review any other systems sharing the META_ACCESS_TOKEN env var.
// CVE-2026-48039 token leak — Graph API URL carrying access_token
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "graph.facebook.com"
| where RemoteUrl has "access_token="
| extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, RemoteUrl)
| extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, RemoteUrl)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, GraphPath, TokenPreview
| union (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "graph.facebook.com" and ProcessCommandLine has "access_token="
    | where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","python.exe","python3.exe")
    | extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, ProcessCommandLine)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName=FileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountName, RemoteIP=tostring(dynamic(null)), RemotePort=toint(0), RemoteUrl=ProcessCommandLine, GraphPath, TokenPreview
)
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 leak — proxy / ASIM web session carrying access_token to graph.facebook.com
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where HttpHostName =~ "graph.facebook.com" or Url has "graph.facebook.com"
| where Url has "access_token="
| extend TokenPreview = extract(@"access_token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]{6,12})", 1, Url)
| extend GraphPath = extract(@"graph\.facebook\.com/(v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", 1, Url)
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname=HttpHostName, Url, GraphPath, TokenPreview, UA=HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| summarize Hits = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), DistinctTokens = dcount(TokenPreview), arg_min(TimeGenerated, *) by SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, DstHostname
| order by FirstSeen desc

Vulnerable meta-ads-mcp installation inventory (CVE-2026-48039) on managed hosts AIReconnaissance High
Inventory-style hunt that surfaces every managed host running meta-ads-mcp (any version), then flags installations at v1.0.108 or earlier as vulnerable to CVE-2026-48039. Pivots on both pip-installed and Docker-deployed instances since the project ships both ways. Rationale: Article specifies the affected version range (`≤ 1.0.101` confirmed, `1.0.102–1.0.105` lacking git tags, package metadata listing `vuln <= 1.0.108`). Pinning to `^1\.0\.(\d|[1-9]\d|10[0-8])$` matches every published vulnerable version while excluding 1.0.109+. Cross-checked against PyPI release listing. Cross-checked against: • https://pypi.org/project/meta-ads-mcp/ • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp
ATT&CKT1592.002 T1518
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer laptops running the package against a sandbox Meta Ads test account (not actually exposed)
  • CI/CD runners installing meta-ads-mcp ephemerally for integration tests
  • Versions strings appearing in pip download cache filenames without an actual running listener
  • Patched 1.0.109+ instances whose container tag still carries an old version label
  • Vendored copies in monorepos where the version string in path doesn't reflect the deployed binary
Response runbook
1) Triage: for each host flagged YES, confirm a live listener exists via `netstat -an | findstr 8080` (or `ss -tlnp` on Linux) and check whether the listener is bound to 0.0.0.0 vs 127.0.0.1. 2) Contain: upgrade vulnerable hosts to meta-ads-mcp v1.0.109+ (once available), or apply the upstream remediation from the advisory (return 401 in `AuthInjectionMiddleware.dispatch()` and strip `access_token` from `request_url`). In the interim, firewall TCP 8080 to internal CIDRs only. 3) Hunt: pivot from each vulnerable host into UC-1 (any inbound /mcp POSTs) and UC-2 (any outbound graph.facebook.com URL carrying access_token) over the past 30 days to assess pre-detection exposure.
// CVE-2026-48039 — inventory hunt for meta-ads-mcp installations
let ProcessSightings = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
    | extend FullCmd = strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, " || ", ProcessCommandLine)
    | extend VersionString = extract(@"meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp[=\s/\-]*([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", 1, FullCmd)
    | extend ContainerImage = extract(@"(meta-ads-mcp[A-Za-z0-9._:-]*)", 1, FullCmd)
    | summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleCmd = any(FullCmd), VersionString = any(VersionString), ContainerImage = any(ContainerImage)
              by DeviceId, DeviceName;
let TVMSightings = DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory
    | where SoftwareName has_any ("meta-ads-mcp", "meta_ads_mcp")
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion;
ProcessSightings
| join kind=fullouter TVMSightings on DeviceId
| extend Version = coalesce(VersionString, SoftwareVersion)
| extend Vulnerable = case(
    isempty(Version), "UNKNOWN",
    Version matches regex @"^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$", "YES (<=1.0.108)",
    "NO"
  )
| project DeviceName = coalesce(DeviceName, DeviceName1), Version, Vulnerable, ContainerImage, SampleCmd, FirstSeen, LastSeen
| order by Vulnerable desc, LastSeen desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — Sentinel inventory hunt for meta-ads-mcp
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(coalesce(ParentProcessCommandLine,""), " || ", coalesce(ActingProcessCommandLine,""))
| extend VersionString = extract(@"meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp[=\s/\-]*([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)", 1, FullCmd)
| extend Vulnerable = case(
    isempty(VersionString), "UNKNOWN",
    VersionString matches regex @"^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$", "YES (<=1.0.108)",
    "NO"
  )
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated), SampleCmd = any(FullCmd), VersionString = any(VersionString), Vulnerable = any(Vulnerable)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername
| order by Vulnerable desc, LastSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:windows.security) (@CommandLine:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp*) OR @process.command_line:(*meta_ads_mcp* OR *meta-ads-mcp*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp/i
| Version := regex("meta[-_]ads[-_]mcp[=\\s/-]*(?<Version>\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+)", field=CommandLine, strict=false)
| Vulnerable := if(Version=/^1\.0\.([0-9]|[1-9][0-9]|10[0-8])$/, then="YES", else="UNKNOWN")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, Version, Vulnerable, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(as=hits), min(@timestamp, as=first_seen), max(@timestamp, as=last_seen)])
| sort(field=Vulnerable, order=desc)

meta-ads-mcp Streamable HTTP listener bound to non-loopback interface AIWeaponization High
Hunts processes invoking meta-ads-mcp where the HTTP transport is bound to a public/non-loopback interface (0.0.0.0 or a routable IP) rather than 127.0.0.1, and Docker `docker run -p` mappings that publish TCP 8080 outside the host loopback. Per the article's own PoC the safe binding is `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080`; anything else exposes the unauthenticated /mcp endpoint to the network. Rationale: The article's PoC uses `docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 ...` — i.e. the safe loopback binding. The dangerous variants (`-p 8080:8080`, `-p 0.0.0.0:8080:8080`, `--host 0.0.0.0`) publish the unauthenticated /mcp endpoint to every network reachable to the host. Detecting the exposed binding lets a SOC reduce the attack surface BEFORE inbound traffic arrives. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp/blob/main/STREAMABLE_HTTP_SETUP.md
ATT&CKT1133 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Intentional internal-only deployment behind a network firewall/segment where 0.0.0.0 binding is fine because the host is unreachable from the internet
  • Kubernetes pods using 0.0.0.0 binding inside the pod network (intentional, fronted by ClusterIP Service)
  • Developer staging containers on isolated bridge networks
  • Reverse-proxy patterns where Nginx fronts the listener on 8080 and enforces auth upstream
  • Operators using `--host ::` (IPv6 wildcard) instead of 0.0.0.0 — this signature misses that case
Suppression filter
and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("kubelet.exe","kubelet") and not (ParentProcessName has_any ("containerd-shim","docker-proxy") and DvcHostname has "k8s-internal")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the listener is actually reachable from outside the host by attempting a connection from a non-trusted network to the host's public/RFC1918 IP on TCP 8080. Look for an upstream reverse proxy enforcing auth. 2) Contain: stop the container/process, restart with `-p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080` (or in Kubernetes, switch the Service from LoadBalancer/NodePort to ClusterIP). Apply network policy/security-group rule blocking 8080 ingress. 3) Hunt: if the listener was reachable, query UC-1 (inbound /mcp POSTs) and UC-2 (graph.facebook.com URL with access_token) for the host's public IP and any private interfaces, going back to the host's first sighting of the vulnerable binary.
// CVE-2026-48039 — meta-ads-mcp listener exposed beyond loopback
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp", "meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, " || ", ProcessCommandLine)
| where FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(--host\s+0\.0\.0\.0|--host\s+\*|0\.0\.0\.0:8080|-p\s+8080:8080(\s|$)|-p\s+0\.0\.0\.0:8080:|--publish[= ]0\.0\.0\.0:8080)"
| where not(FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(127\.0\.0\.1:8080:8080|-p\s+127\.0\.0\.1:8080|--host\s+127\.0\.0\.1|--host\s+localhost)")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — meta-ads-mcp exposed listener via process create
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp")
| extend FullCmd = strcat(coalesce(ParentProcessCommandLine,""), " || ", coalesce(ActingProcessCommandLine,""))
| where FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(--host\s+0\.0\.0\.0|--host\s+\*|0\.0\.0\.0:8080|-p\s+8080:8080(\s|$)|-p\s+0\.0\.0\.0:8080:|--publish[= ]0\.0\.0\.0:8080)"
| where not(FullCmd matches regex @"(?i)(127\.0\.0\.1:8080:8080|-p\s+127\.0\.0\.1:8080|--host\s+127\.0\.0\.1|--host\s+localhost)")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

CVE-2026-48039 PoC artifact execution (meta-ads-mcp-vuln001 image, FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO env) AIExploitation High
Hunts the exact PoC artifacts published with the advisory: a Docker image tagged `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001`, the `META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789` env-var literal, and a `poc.py` exploit script run from an interactive shell. Hits indicate an analyst, red-teamer, or attacker actively rehearsing the PoC inside the environment. Rationale: PoC strings are pulled verbatim from the article — the docker invocation `docker run --rm -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -e META_ACCESS_TOKEN=FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO_123456789 meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` and the `python3 poc.py` runner. The image tag `meta-ads-mcp-vuln001` and the FAKE_TOKEN literal have no legitimate use outside reproducing the advisory PoC, so hits should be treated as either (a) authorised purple-team activity or (b) attacker rehearsal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.006 T1610
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security team rehearsing the PoC in a sandbox — should be allowlisted by host or by tagged session
  • Vulnerability-management vendors running their own validation harness against staging
  • Security-research blog post readers copy-pasting the PoC on their workstation
  • Generic poc.py filenames unrelated to this CVE (filtered out by the meta-ads-mcp / graph.facebook.com co-occurrence requirement)
  • Container image-scanning pipelines pulling the image for SBOM analysis (filter by parent image-scanner process)
Suppression filter
and DvcHostname !startswith "redteam-" and DvcHostname !startswith "vulnscan-" and ActorUsername !in~ ("svc-purpleteam","redteam-runner")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether the host belongs to the security team's red-team / vuln-research fleet (check asset tags). If unknown, capture the full process tree and any inbound/outbound network connections from the same host in a ±15-minute window. 2) Contain: isolate the host via EDR network containment if it's NOT a sanctioned research host. Snapshot disk + memory for forensics. Revoke any Meta access tokens that share the host's environment (in case real tokens were also tested). 3) Hunt: pivot on the operator account that ran the PoC — query for any access to internal meta-ads-mcp servers (UC-1 inbound /mcp), graph.facebook.com URLs carrying access_token (UC-2), and lateral movement from this host in the same session; review git history on the host for clones of pipeboard-co/meta-ads-mcp.
// CVE-2026-48039 — PoC artefacts (docker image, fake token literal, poc.py exploit)
let ProcMatches = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ProcessCommandLine has "meta-ads-mcp-vuln001"
         or ProcessCommandLine has "FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO"
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "meta-ads-mcp-vuln001"
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO"
         or (ProcessCommandLine has "poc.py" and (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","graph.facebook.com","/mcp","tools/call","get_ad_accounts")))
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "process";
let FileMatches = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "poc.py"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","code.exe","pwsh.exe","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","explorer.exe","curl.exe","git.exe")
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","GHSA-9gw6-46qc-99vr","CVE-2026-48039")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine = "", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "file";
union ProcMatches, FileMatches
| order by Timestamp desc
// CVE-2026-48039 — PoC artefacts via ASIM
let ProcMatches = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
         or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta-ads-mcp-vuln001","FAKE_TOKEN_FOR_POC_DEMO")
         or (ActingProcessCommandLine has "poc.py" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("meta_ads_mcp","meta-ads-mcp","graph.facebook.com","/mcp","tools/call","get_ad_accounts"))
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, Source="process";
let FileMatches = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where TargetFileName =~ "poc.py"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","code","pwsh","powershell","bash","git","curl")
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, Source="file";
union ProcMatches, FileMatches
| order by TimeGenerated desc
